title: Demazure reflection sequences with affine-root error characters
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], with these terms as defined in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq S$, with $B$ a Borel subgroup, and use $X=X^*(T)$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and their pairing from [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $B^-$ be the Borel opposite to $B$ relative to $T$, so its roots are $-\Phi^+$. Put $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$, $Q=\mathbf Z\Phi$, and $W=N_S(T)(F)/T(F)$, acting on $X$ by normalizer conjugation. Set $w\mathbin\cdot x=w(x+\rho)-\rho$, let $w_0\Phi^+=-\Phi^+$, and put $N=|\Phi^+|$. A rational module for any group here is an $F$-vector space with a coassociative counital coaction into its tensor product with that group's coordinate algebra; a submodule is a coaction-stable subspace. For $x\in X$, let $F_x$ be the one-dimensional $B^-$-module on which $T$ acts by $x$ and the unipotent radical acts trivially. For a finite-dimensional rational $B^-$-module $M$, let $\mathcal L(M)$ be the sheaf of sections of $S\times^{B^-}M$ on $S/B^-$: over $V\subseteq S/B^-$ its sections are regular maps $f:\pi^{-1}(V)\to M$ with $f(gb)=b^{-1}f(g)$, where $\pi:S\to S/B^-$ is the quotient. Write $H^i(M)=H^i(S/B^-,\mathcal L(M))$ for Zariski sheaf cohomology, with its natural left $S$-action, and $H^i(x)=H^i(F_x)$; set $H^i=0$ for $i<0$. Equivariance means a coaction identity, hence holds after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. A simple module is nonzero with no proper nonzero rational submodule, and a simple constituent means a simple subquotient. Fix $\alpha\in\Delta$ and $x\in X$ with $r=\langle x+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ge0$, and put $\zeta=x+\rho$. Let $P_\alpha$ be the minimal parabolic generated by $B^-$ and the root subgroup of root $\alpha$, as in [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-line-cohomology]. For $r>0$ let $V_\alpha^\zeta=H^0(P_\alpha/B^-,\mathcal L(F_\zeta))$, let $K_\alpha^\zeta$ be the kernel of evaluation at the identity coset $V_\alpha^\zeta\to F_\zeta$, and let $\overline V_\alpha^\zeta=K_\alpha^\zeta/F_{s_\alpha\zeta}$. In the rank-one weight basis $e_0^\zeta,\ldots,e_r^\zeta$ normalized as in [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-line-cohomology], the rule $\overline e_i^\zeta\mapsto i e_{i-1}^{\zeta-\alpha}$ for $1\le i\le r-1$ defines a $B^-$-linear map $d:\overline V_\alpha^\zeta\to V_\alpha^{\zeta-\alpha}$. When $r=1$, the target denotes the zero fibre-cohomology module of degree $-1$. Put $C_\alpha^\zeta=\ker d$, $J_\alpha^\zeta=\operatorname{im}d$, and $Q_\alpha^\zeta=\operatorname{coker}d$. There are exact sequences
$$0\to K_\alpha^\zeta\to V_\alpha^\zeta\to F_\zeta\to0,\quad 0\to F_{s_\alpha\zeta}\to K_\alpha^\zeta\to\overline V_\alpha^\zeta\to0,$$
$$0\to C_\alpha^\zeta\to\overline V_\alpha^\zeta\to J_\alpha^\zeta\to0,\quad0\to J_\alpha^\zeta\to V_\alpha^{\zeta-\alpha}\to Q_\alpha^\zeta\to0.$$
Both $C_\alpha^\zeta$ and $Q_\alpha^\zeta$ have precisely the weights $s_\alpha\zeta+kp\alpha$ with integers $0<kp<r$, each once. Write $E=\overline V_\alpha^\zeta\otimes F_{-\rho}$, $C=C_\alpha^\zeta\otimes F_{-\rho}$, $Q'=Q_\alpha^\zeta\otimes F_{-\rho}$. The preceding sequences induce an $S$-equivariant long exact sequence containing, for every integer $i$,
$$\cdots\longrightarrow H^i(E)\longrightarrow H^{i+1}(s_\alpha\mathbin\cdot x)\longrightarrow H^i(x)\longrightarrow H^{i+1}(E)\longrightarrow H^{i+2}(s_\alpha\mathbin\cdot x)\longrightarrow\cdots,$$
and $S$-equivariant exact segments
$$H^{i+1}(C)\longrightarrow H^{i+1}(E)\longrightarrow H^i(Q').$$
Every weight of $C$ or $Q'$ has the form $s_\alpha\mathbin\cdot x+kp\alpha$ with $0<kp<r$. For $r=0$, all $H^i(x)$ and $H^i(s_\alpha\mathbin\cdot x)$ are zero and the same exact segments hold with $E=C=Q'=0$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit], $\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=1$. Consequently $\langle-\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=-1$, $\langle\zeta-\alpha,\alpha^\vee\rangle=r-2$, and $s_\alpha\zeta-\rho=s_\alpha\mathbin\cdot x$. These identities determine the twists and degrees used below.

proof.text: Use the weight bases and simple-root action of [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-line-cohomology]. All the other negative root groups act trivially on each of these section modules. Here is the coefficient check: write $u_{-\beta}(z)v=\sum_{n\ge0}z^n v_n$ for a vector of weight $\lambda$. The conjugation identity in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] gives $t v_n=(\lambda-n\beta)(t)v_n$ by comparison of coefficients in $F[T][z]$, and the identity at $z=0$ gives $v_0=v$. All weights of either section module differ by integer multiples of $\alpha$. For $\beta\in\Phi^+\setminus\{\alpha\}$, reducedness of the root system in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] implies $n\beta\notin\mathbf Z\alpha$ for $n>0$. Thus all $v_n$ with $n>0$ vanish. This is a polynomial/coaction identity, including the terms of degree divisible by $p$. Finally [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], applied with Borel $B^-$ and positive system $-\Phi^+$, together with $B^-=R_u(B^-)\rtimes T$ from the Borel-pair node, shows that an intertwining identity on $T$ and $U_{-\alpha}$ suffices for these modules.

proof.text: Suppose $r>0$. Evaluation $\operatorname{ev}:V_\alpha^\zeta\to F_\zeta$ is $B^-$-linear: for a section $f$ and $b\in B^-$, $(bf)(1)=f(b^{-1})=b f(1)$. It is nonzero. Indeed if it were zero, every section would satisfy $f(g)=\operatorname{ev}(g^{-1}f)=0$ on $P_\alpha$ as a regular-map identity, contradicting the nonzero module of dimension $r+1$ given by [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-line-cohomology]. The distinct basis weights $s_\alpha\zeta+i\alpha$ imply that evaluation kills $e_0^\zeta,\ldots,e_{r-1}^\zeta$ and is nonzero on $e_r^\zeta$; rescale the whole basis if needed. Hence $K_\alpha^\zeta$ is exactly their span. Its line $F e_0^\zeta$ has weight $s_\alpha\zeta$ and is fixed by $U_{-\alpha}$ by the displayed binomial formula. The other negative root groups act trivially by step 2. Thus this line is $F_{s_\alpha\zeta}$ as a $B^-$-module. Taking the kernel and then this quotient gives the first two short exact sequences, and $\overline V_\alpha^\zeta$ has basis $\overline e_1^\zeta,\ldots,\overline e_{r-1}^\zeta$.

proof.text:
For $r\ge2$ write $f_j=e_j^{\zeta-\alpha}$, $0\le j\le r-2$. Use one coordinate $u_{-\alpha}$ for both modules: any other isomorphism $\mathbf G_a\cong U_{-\alpha}$ is $z\mapsto u_{-\alpha}(cz)$ with $c\in F^\times$, since a group automorphism of $\mathbf G_a$ over a field is an additive polynomial with polynomial inverse, hence of degree one. If a basis $e_i$ satisfies the binomial formula for $u_{-\alpha}(c\,\cdot)$, then $c^ie_i$ satisfies it for $u_{-\alpha}$ and has the same weights; so both bases below are taken for the same $u_{-\alpha}$. By [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-line-cohomology] and the reflection formula in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], its weight is $s_\alpha(\zeta-\alpha)+j\alpha=s_\alpha\zeta+(j+1)\alpha$, the weight of $\overline e_{j+1}^\zeta$. Thus $d(\overline e_i^\zeta)=i f_{i-1}$ commutes with $T$. For the simple negative root group the two sides are
$$d(u_{-\alpha}(z)\overline e_i)=\sum_{j=1}^{i}j\binom{i}{j}z^{i-j}f_{j-1},\qquad u_{-\alpha}(z)d(\overline e_i)=\sum_{j=1}^{i}i\binom{i-1}{j-1}z^{i-j}f_{j-1}.$$
The integer identity $j\binom{i}{j}=i\binom{i-1}{j-1}$ proves equality in every $F$-algebra, including characteristic $p$. The remaining root groups are trivial by step 2, so $d$ is $B^-$-linear. For $r=1$, both source and target are zero and the same assertion holds for the unique zero map.

proof.text: In the bases of steps 3--4 the matrix of $d$ is diagonal with entries $1,2,\ldots,r-1$ in $F$. Its kernel therefore has basis $\overline e_i$ for $0<i<r$ and $p\mid i$, and its cokernel has basis the classes of $f_{i-1}$ for exactly those indices. Both lists have weight $s_\alpha\zeta+i\alpha$. Distinct indices have distinct character weights because $X$ is torsion-free and $\alpha\ne0$. This proves the claimed weights, each with multiplicity one. Defining $C_\alpha^\zeta=\ker d$, $J_\alpha^\zeta=\operatorname{im}d$, $Q_\alpha^\zeta=\operatorname{coker}d$ gives the last two short exact sequences. Kernels and images are stable because $d$ is a coaction morphism; the cokernel has the induced coaction. Tensoring with $F_{-\rho}$ simply subtracts $\rho$ from each weight, yielding $s_\alpha\mathbin\cdot x+kp\alpha$ with $0<kp<r$. Tensoring is exact since it is tensoring a vector space with a one-dimensional vector space.

proof.text:
Put $A=V_\alpha^\zeta\otimes F_{-\rho}$, $D=V_\alpha^{\zeta-\alpha}\otimes F_{-\rho}$, and $K_t=K_\alpha^\zeta\otimes F_{-\rho}$. By [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-line-cohomology], both $A$ and $D$ have zero cohomology in every degree: their untwisted factors are rational $P_\alpha$-modules and the twist pairs to $-1$. For $r=1$ the second factor is zero, so $D=0$ directly. The long exact sequence of $0\to K_t\to A\to F_x\to0$ from [lem-sfb-flag-cohomology-finite-exact] identifies $\delta:H^i(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{i+1}(K_t)$. Substituting its inverse into the long exact sequence of $0\to F_{s_\alpha\cdot x}\to K_t\to E\to0$ gives precisely
$$\cdots\to H^i(E)\to H^{i+1}(s_\alpha\cdot x)\to H^i(x)\to H^{i+1}(E)\to H^{i+2}(s_\alpha\cdot x)\to\cdots.$$
The arrow into $H^i(x)$ is the map into $H^{i+1}(K_t)$ followed by $\delta^{-1}$; the arrow out is $\delta$ followed by the map into $H^{i+1}(E)$. Thus exactness is preserved. The cited long exact sequences and connecting maps are $S$-equivariant; inverses of equivariant isomorphisms are equivariant. At the left boundary $H^0(K_t)=0$ by its injection into $H^0(A)=0$, so these identifications also hold with the zero convention for negative degrees.

proof.text:
Write $J_t=J_\alpha^\zeta\otimes F_{-\rho}$. Apply [lem-sfb-flag-cohomology-finite-exact] to $0\to J_t\to D\to Q'\to0$. Since $H^*(D)=0$ by step 6, its connecting map gives $\epsilon:H^i(Q')\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{i+1}(J_t)$. The cohomology sequence of $0\to C\to E\to J_t\to0$ then gives
$$H^{i+1}(C)\longrightarrow H^{i+1}(E)\longrightarrow H^i(Q'),$$
where the second arrow is $H^{i+1}(E)\to H^{i+1}(J_t)$ followed by $\epsilon^{-1}$. It is exact at the middle term, and all arrows are $S$-equivariant. For $i=-1$ the same assertion uses $H^0(J_t)=0$, which follows by injection into $H^0(D)=0$; for lower $i$ all terms are zero. This also explains explicitly the boundary-degree interpretation of the stated exact segments.

proof.text: If $r=0$, step 1 gives $\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle=-1$, and $s_\alpha\zeta=\zeta$ gives $s_\alpha\cdot x=x$. Apply the last acyclicity clause of [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-line-cohomology] with the trivial one-dimensional $P_\alpha$-module $V=F$ and $\mu=x$. It gives $H^i(x)=0$ for all $i\ge0$, and hence the same for $s_\alpha\cdot x$. Set $E=C=Q'=0$ as required. Every term of both displayed cohomology sequences is now zero. Negative degrees are zero by the stated convention.
